title: Merge two sorted lists
instructorPromptText: Write a C function `void merge_sorted_arrays(const int *arr1, int size1, const int *arr2, int size2, int *merged)` that merges two sorted integer arrays into a single sorted array in linear O(N) time (do not merge and re-sort).

specGateDimensions.description: Does the function merge elements in linear time (O(N1 + N2)) using a single pass with two indices, rather than copying all elements and calling a sorting function?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Verifies understanding of array traversal efficiency; merging pre-sorted datasets is a key algorithm demonstrating scale awareness.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the function have clean loops to copy the trailing elements from whichever array was not fully exhausted?
specGateDimensions.rationale: When one array is exhausted, the loop exits. The student must check both arrays and copy any remaining elements to `merged`.

specGateDimensions.description: Are the source pointer/index variables advanced conditionally based on which element was smaller and copied?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Mismatched index updates (e.g. incrementing `j` when copying from `arr1[i]`) lead to duplicated elements and garbage data.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student copies elements to the target array and then runs a bubble sort or qsort, violating the linear-time requirement.
Student terminates the merge once the shorter array is exhausted, leaving the rest of the longer array uncopied.
Student uses pointer navigation (incrementing `arr1`, `arr2`, and `merged` pointers directly) instead of using integer index brackets.
Student increments the incorrect pointer or index variable, copying garbage values or skipping elements.
Student allocates the merged array inside the function and returns its pointer instead of writing into the output buffer parameter.
